chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm al-Hāshimī, from his grandfather Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Sulaymān al-Jaʿfarī, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a Prophet from among the Prophets: “When I am obeyed, I am pleased; and when I am pleased, I bless, and there is no end to My blessing. And when I am disobeyed, I become wrathful; and when I become wrathful, I curse, and My curse reaches the seventh among the progeny.”

key_terms.الْوَرَى: the created beings; here, the progeny or descendants among mankind
key_terms.بَارَكْتُ: I bestowed barakah; I granted blessing and increase
key_terms.بَرَكَتِي: My barakah; Allah’s blessing that has no limit
key_terms.رَضِيتُ: I became pleased; Allah’s pleasure in response to obedience
key_terms.غَضِبْتُ: I became wrathful in response to disobedience
key_terms.لَعَنْتُ: I cursed; I expelled from divine mercy
key_terms.لَعْنَتِي: My curse; divine rejection and distancing from mercy

ai.seo_question: How does obedience to Allah bring barakah, and what are the consequences of disobedience?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that obedience to Allah leads to His pleasure, and His pleasure brings boundless barakah. It also warns that disobedience brings divine wrath and laʿnah, with consequences that can extend through generations.
